subject.title: Bounded memory tool with hard character limits

question: Should OpenClaw add a first-class bounded memory CRUD write contract to memory-core, and if so what hard-limit, identity, duplicate/consolidation, config, snapshot, and secret-handling semantics should it expose?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but implementing it would create new public memory-write, configuration, persistence, and sensitive-data behavior that automation should not choose without maintainer intent.

options.title: Define Memory-Core Bounded CRUD
options.body: Adopt this as a memory-core design track and specify add/list/replace/remove, capacity feedback, limit enforcement, identity, duplicate handling, snapshot behavior, and secret policy before code lands.

options.title: Narrow To Existing Flush Paths
options.body: Keep first-class CRUD out of core for now and address bloat only through memory-flush, promotion, bounded read, and recall surfaces.

options.title: Prototype Externally First
options.body: Ask contributors to prototype the write policy as a memory plugin or ClawHub package until a missing core/plugin API gap is proven.

recommendation.title: Define Memory-Core Bounded CRUD
recommendation.body: Adopt this as a memory-core design track and specify add/list/replace/remove, capacity feedback, limit enforcement, identity, duplicate handling, snapshot behavior, and secret policy before code lands.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest visible history across memory-core ownership, pre-compaction memory flush, and plugin-boundary refactors that govern this product/API decision.
